items: Compression: the particles of a solid are closely packed and cannot move closer, unlike those of a gas. In metallic solids the atoms are spherically symmetrical and pack into hexagonal and cubic close-packed structures in which the particles touch but, being spheres, cannot fill more than 74 per cent of the space; compression of solids is not possible.

Expansion: expansion increases the spaces between particles, but in solids the forces of attraction are so strong that a rise in temperature hardly affects their relative positions; the particles vibrate about their mean positions and the volume hardly increases. Coefficients of linear and cubic expansion exist but are negligible compared with liquids and gases.
Motion of particles: the particles of a solid undergo neither translatory nor rotational motion; they only vibrate about their mean positions, more intensely at higher temperature.
Inter-particle space: the spaces are far less than in liquids because of the stronger forces, so solids are mostly hard, with high melting points and high stability.
Inter-particle forces: the particles are held by ionic, covalent, metallic or van der Waals forces, strong enough to fix them in place and allow only vibration.
Kinetic energy: since solid particles have only vibratory motion, the only kinetic energy a solid possesses is vibrational kinetic energy.

blocks.prompt: Why do solids have very low compressibility and expansion, and why do their particles not undergo translatory motion?
blocks.explanation: The particles are already touching, so there is no empty space to squeeze out, and the attractive forces are so strong that heating only makes the particles vibrate a little more widely without changing their positions. The same strong forces lock each particle at its place in the structure, so it cannot travel through the solid; it can only vibrate about its mean position.

items: Solids: no compression (close packing, spheres fill at most 74 per cent), negligible expansion, vibration only (no translation or rotation), least inter-particle space, held by ionic, covalent, metallic or van der Waals forces, only vibrational kinetic energy.
